comparator.name: Animal Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: Full current2026–2027 BAS common compulsory cluster totals111EC, plus3EC conditional mathematics/statistics and12EC thesis=126commonEC. SpecA has18EC compulsory plus6EC restricted choice, selecting first listed YAS33406 independently of UCR fit.30genuine elective EC close180. Complete57B1common+3ECMathA-preparation choice=60B1, then42B2common+18SpecA=60B2; complete12B3common+6restricted+12thesis+30electives=60B3. YAS21303 is a continuous3EC portfolio concluded alongside thesis; YAS21400 and general/lab/fieldwork safety are additional0EC obligations, not omitted credit awards. Thesis formal intake requires102compulsory/restricted credits including all60B1; AdvancedStatistics and SkillsAcademy before or alongside thesis. Use current API module requirements;2025scheme and2020–2021guide are historical cross-checks, not controlling requirements. The original generic/misnamed components and42EC mixed elective/specialisation bucket are replaced with exact current modules and genuine30ECelectives.

components.name: Zoology (English)
components.note: UCR Functional Anatomy studies human anatomy. WUR’s Zoology additionally develops comparative vertebrate form, evolution/development, histology and animal practicals.

components.name: General Chemistry for the Life Sciences
Dilemmas in Animal Management and Care
Animal Behaviour
components.note: UCR Neurobiology includes animal behaviour, welfare and comparative neural mechanisms. WUR adds dedicated ethological observation, Tinbergen’s questions and behavioural-data collection.

components.name: Internship
components.note: WUR requires practical animal handling, feeding and housing training plus an individual husbandry internship. The UCR classroom/laboratory courses do not supply this placement.

components.name: Human and Animal Physiology
components.note: Normal organ-system regulation is shared. UCR focuses on human physiology; WUR includes comparative animal morphology, histology and physiological practicals.

components.name: Immunology and Thermoregulation
components.note: Shared host-defence and inflammatory mechanisms are a partial correspondence. WUR additionally integrates animal housing/climate stress, immunology and thermoregulation.

components.name: Veterinary Epidemiology and Economics
components.note: Epidemiological risk/design/causality methods are shared; UCR studies human public health, while WUR integrates animal disease-control decisions and veterinary economics.

components.name: Principles of Animal Nutrition
components.note: Biochemistry shares nutrient chemistry and energy metabolism. WUR adds animal-specific requirements, feed formulation/manufacture, chemical feed/faeces analysis and live-animal trials.

components.name: Skills Academy and Personal Assessment
components.note: Skills Academy is a 3 EC continuous portfolio across all 3 years, concluding alongside the thesis. UCR’s PPD develops shared academic/reflection skills in Year 1; the structures differ.

components.name: Quantitative Skills for Animal Sciences
components.note: Exploratory data preparation, visualisation and R scripting are shared. WUR additionally connects advanced statistical models and assumption checks to animal data and uses Excel.

components.name: Mathematics Applied: Introduction
components.note: This example selects Mathematics Applied: Introduction for VWO Mathematics A. Students with Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead; other educational backgrounds choose with the study adviser.

components.name: Aquaculture Biology
components.note: UCR Marine Biology studies ecosystems, fisheries/aquaculture and human impacts; it does not reproduce the cultivation physiology and practicals required by Aquaculture Biology.

components.name: Introduction to Business Economics, Management and Marketing
Role of Livestock in Future Food Systems
components.note: This example chooses Role of Livestock in Future Food Systems from the 6 EC restricted cluster. Fish/seafood sustainability or Companion Animals are alternatives, not added requirements.

components.name: BSc Thesis Animal Sciences
components.note: WUR requires an individual 12 EC animal-sciences thesis with proposal, research, written report, presentation and defence. Formal intake requires 102 compulsory/restricted credits including all 60 first-year credits; Advanced Statistics and Skills Academy are taken before or alongside the thesis. Optional UCR 15 EC independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 EC.

components.name: Minor and/or individually chosen electives
components.note: The pathway retains 30 EC for a minor and/or individually chosen electives. No specific minor is added to the required courses shown here.

alternatives.concept: Combine animal diversity, evolution, ecology and comparative neurobiology with cellular biology, metabolism, physiology, immunity and evidence about disease. Use farming, life-cycle assessment, ethics and sustainability governance to examine animal welfare and animal–environment relationships. Human biomedical study contributes shared mechanisms without replacing species-specific husbandry.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Each course has its required gateway completed in an earlier term and every assigned offering is planned for the fixed Fall2026 cohort. The plans develop biological or ecological foundations before advanced applications. Cell biology precedes molecular pathology/genetics, physiology precedes pharmacology, empirical statistics precedes meta-analysis and introductory R data work precedes machine learning where selected.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three sequentially tested material related responses: animal-related biological/ecological mechanisms and welfare; molecular physiology/disease/evidence synthesis; animal ecology/farming/environmental assessment and enterprise. The unimplemented Foods of Animal Origin direction remains separately owned; no professional or disciplinary equivalence claimed.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Shared cell structure, membranes, signalling, gene regulation and bioenergetics. WUR includes its own cell/biochemical laboratory practicals; UCR’s Molecular Cell Biology emphasises molecular mechanisms and research appraisal.

Shared normal mammalian homeostasis, endocrine/nervous control and integrated organ-system function. UCR focuses on humans; WUR includes comparative animal morphology, histology and physiology practicals.

Shared biomolecular nutrient chemistry, enzyme function and energy/nitrogen metabolism. WUR additionally teaches animal-specific requirements, diet formulation/processing, feed analysis and live-animal trials.

Shared mammalian anatomical structure–function reasoning and study of skeletal/organ material. UCR studies human anatomy; WUR develops comparative vertebrate anatomy, evolution/development, histology and animal physiological practicals.

Shared innate/adaptive host defence, inflammation and disease-resistance mechanisms. WUR integrates environmental stress and animal thermoregulation; UCR includes host-pathogen mechanisms and flow-cytometry-data analysis.

Shared animal behaviour, evolutionary/neural mechanisms, welfare and ethical research appraisal. WUR additionally teaches a dedicated ethological/Tinbergen framework and collects/analyses behavioural observations.

Shared chemical equilibrium, molecular/energy principles and thermodynamics. UCR uses environmental/material contexts and does not reproduce the complete life-science buffer, kinetics and ATP-coupling sequence.

Shared ethical theory/argument and independent position on practical moral responsibility, including animal-rights applications at UCR. WUR specifically analyses animal management practices and their welfare/sustainability dilemmas.
No selected course integrates the full animal-sciences orientation across species, behaviour/ecology, production and health. Shared cellular/ecological contributions remain separately identified.
No selected course reproduces domestic-animal production biology, live-animal phenotype measurements, feeding/housing, lactation and comparative practical cases.
No adequate whole counterpart for bio-organic reactions, stereochemistry and natural-product structure/reactivity. Biochemistry is most strongly aligned to nutrient metabolism.
Required practical handling/feeding/housing training and individual animal-husbandry internship are not replaced by classroom biology or a community project.
Evolutionary and human genetic mechanisms do not reproduce designing and optimising livestock/companion-animal breeding programmes.
Marine ecology and aquaculture topics are relevant but do not reproduce aquatic-animal cultivation physiology, feeding/growth/reproduction and practicals.
General human reproductive anatomy/physiology does not reproduce farm/companion-species fertility cycles, management and reproductive technologies.
The additional animal-management/inflammation/metabolic/behavioural disorder sequence remains separate; shared host defence is aligned to Immunology and Thermoregulation.

Shared Mendelian, population/quantitative and evolutionary genetics, variation and selection. WUR additionally develops detailed molecular genetic problems and case exercises; UCR develops broader evolutionary history and Tinbergen analysis.

Shared environmental conditions/resources, population dynamics, predation, competition and food webs, with quantitative ecological modelling. WUR focuses on animals, ecological-requirement projects and wildlife observation.

Shared environmental/social appraisal of animal husbandry, aquaculture, alternative proteins and farming innovations. WUR specifically compares competing livestock-food-system narratives, planetary/human/animal health and feed–food/circularity dilemmas.

Shared sustainability assessment, production-system impacts and circular-resource reasoning. WUR integrates systems/linear-programming and qualitative methods in a livestock case; UCR develops product/process life-cycle assessment.
Shared business-environment analysis, marketing/finance/operations and an integrated business plan. WUR applies planning to a food-supply-chain enterprise; UCR develops a new-venture concept.

Shared academic writing/presentation, personal goals, reflection and collaboration. UCR is a Year1 course with civic engagement; WUR’s3EC SkillsAcademy runs across all3years and concludes alongside the thesis.
Shared disease frequency, causal reasoning, epidemiological designs, risk and outbreak analysis. UCR is human public health; WUR adds animal-population disease control and economic decision methods.

Shared differentiation, integration, differential equations and mathematical modelling. UCR adds dynamic population/predator–prey modelling; the prior-preparation introduction and separate linear-algebra award remain distinct.

Shared statistical estimation, confidence intervals and hypothesis testing, grounded in probability and simulation at UCR. WUR additionally develops simple applied regression for life-science data; the advanced-statistics award remains separate.
Shared exploratory analysis, data preparation/visualisation and R scripting/reporting. WUR connects advanced statistical-model building/checks specifically to animal data and also uses Excel.
Shared multiple regression, ANOVA/ANCOVA, categorical/repeated-measures models, assumptions and R-based data interpretation. Applications and exact inferential scope differ.
No selected dedicated vectors/matrices/eigenvalues/linear-algebra course; current Mathematical Methods detailed content is calculus/dynamic modelling.
This prior-preparation-dependent3EC introduction remains separate; UCR Mathematical Methods is aligned once to the stronger applied-analysis component.

Required individual animal-sciences research, proposal, original data analysis, thesis, presentation and defence have no taught-course counterpart. Optional UCR independent research is a separate opportunity outside the24courses/180EC.
Genuine30EC minor/elective space has no specified subject counterpart.

notes.text: UCR can combine substantive animal-related ecology, evolution, comparative neurobiology, sustainable farming and shared biological mechanisms. Its biomedical courses largely study humans. WUR adds dedicated domestic-animal production biology, nutrition/feed practicals, breeding, fertility, aquaculture physiology, animal handling and husbandry internship, and a required animal-sciences thesis. These related UCR programmes do not reproduce that specialist sequence. Optional 15 EC independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: WUR’s English-taught Animal Sciences bachelor studies domesticated and wild animals, from cells and physiological mechanisms to behaviour, welfare, ecology and sustainable production. Animal Management and Care emphasises animals in their environment and society, including nutrition, reproduction, housing and management.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme combines animal-related biology, ecology and welfare with shared biomedical mechanisms. The second deepens molecular physiology, disease and research methods; the third combines animal ecology and sustainable farming with environmental assessment, governance and enterprise. WUR provides more specialised animal nutrition, breeding, fertility, aquaculture physiology and hands-on husbandry. Human biomedical study contributes shared mechanisms and does not replace species-specific training. WUR’s individual thesis is required; UCR’s optional independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 credits.
